sections.name: Core Value Propositions
sections.why: 9 propositions, each with Feature / Benefit / Conversion Angle filled. Specifics (3,500+ tests, 100+ ATS, credit model, 24-month lock, 1,500+ experts) all read as sourced from the pool. No bracket placeholders. Fairness language stays on 'reduces adverse impact', never absolute.

sections.name: Technical Features
sections.why: Five named categories (Assessments & Test Library, Assessment Building & Question Types, Interviewing, Anti-Cheating & Proctoring, Reporting/Analytics/Fairness, plus Branding/Admin/Security) and the proctoring set is enumerated in full by category rather than summarised. Per-use prices ($0.25 / $0.50 / $5) match the add-on table, so no invented specifics.

sections.name: Integrations & Ecosystem
sections.why: Grouped by category with named platforms and a one-line role for each. Zapier-included and white-label-native caveats stated once. Nothing here looks conjured; the long tail (Rena, 8xpand, ATS Anywhere) is too specific to be invented.

sections.name: Competitive Differentiators
sections.why: Eleven named rivals, each with a fair note on rival strength. The two blocks built from Testlify-side facts only (HackerRank/Codility, HireVue) carry explicit HUMAN DECISION flags, which is the legitimate handling. Indeed block even concedes parity items and a genuine Indeed advantage.

sections.name: Use Cases by Customer Segment
sections.why: Seven segments plus eight industry verticals, each tied to named tests and real plan numbers rather than generic persona prose. Above the 3-5 target, but coverage is the completeness test and the extra segments are distinct, not padded.

sections.name: Pricing & Plan Benefits
sections.why: Five real tiers with list and annual prices, credit counts, seat counts, extra-credit rates, plus the model itself (one credit on start, no rollover, 24-month base lock with the add-on carve-out stated). Add-ons and per-use fees listed once, consistent with the proctoring section.

sections.name: Key Messaging for Conversions
sections.why: CONSOLIDATION failure: the same fact carries two conflicting values inside one section. Social Proof says 'G2 High Performer and Leader... 4.8 customer satisfaction' and then, two lines later, 'G2 rating 4.7 across 500+ reviews, the highest among listed alternatives'. The 4.7 figure is also the one used in the Maki People comparison. One G2 number must survive.
sections.redo: Pick the canonical G2 rating (4.7, since it is the sourced figure repeated in the Maki People block with its comparison set) and delete the competing 4.8 claim, or relabel 4.8 explicitly as a different metric with its own source. Also collapse the two overlapping proof bullets into one: '55% decrease in time to hire' and 'Cuts screening workload by up to 75%' each appear both in Pain Point Solutions and again in Social Proof.

sections.name: Common Questions & Objections
sections.why: Sixteen objections covering cheating, AI fairness, price lock, credit expiry, ATS, security, branding, candidate effort. The fairness answer explicitly states 'We say reduce bias, not eliminate it', which is the right posture. Answers restate facts from earlier sections but in answer form, which is the section's job, not duplication.

sections.name: Content Creation Guidelines
sections.why: Eight actionable rules, each with concrete instruction rather than sentiment. Rule 8 names the banned fairness phrasings outright, which is what keeps the rest of the doc legally clean.

redo_notes: One blocking defect. Key Messaging for Conversions states the G2 rating twice with different numbers (4.8 in the G2 Leader line, 4.7 in the alternatives line). Keep 4.7 as canonical, since it is the version carried in the Maki People comparison with its full competitor set, and cut the 4.8 claim unless it can be sourced as a separate metric. While in that section, deduplicate the 55% time-to-hire and 75% screening-workload figures, which each appear in both Pain Point Solutions and Social Proof. Non-blocking tidy elsewhere: in Technical Features > Reporting, the bullet 'AI-powered insights and scoring; AI-driven scoring system; automated scoring; weighted scoring' uses four labels for two capabilities; keep the most specific pair.
